title: NY State Assembly · District 55
area: Brooklyn: Brownsville, Ocean Hill, and parts of East New York

context.text: Incumbent Latrice Walker is unopposed in the general election. The Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled, and Walker advanced without appearing on the ballot in either. Yahemia Harris, who had planned to run on a "No Kings Party" line (and had also filed to run in the Republican primary), is listed by Ballotpedia as a withdrawn or disqualified candidate and does not appear on the November 3 general-election ballot.

summary.text: Latrice Walker is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for Assembly District 55, first elected in 2014. An attorney, she chairs the Assembly's Election Law Committee and is best known for sponsoring New York's 2019 bail reform law. She is unopposed in the November 2026 general election.

background.text: Walker was born and raised in Ocean Hill-Brownsville, Brooklyn, and grew up in the Prospect Plaza Houses, a NYCHA development; she still lives in Ocean Hill-Brownsville.
She is a graduate of Pace University School of Law and worked as an attorney representing people targeted by the NYPD's use of stop-and-frisk and tenants, including NYCHA residents, facing eviction.
Before her election to the Assembly, she worked as counsel to U.S. Representative Yvette Clarke.
She has represented the 55th Assembly District since 2015. She chairs the Assembly's Election Law Committee and also serves on the Housing, Judiciary, Codes, and Ways and Means committees.

priorities.text: Voting rights and election administration: she chairs the Assembly's Election Law Committee and has sponsored bills on protections against illegal voter purging, modernized voter registration, and related election-law measures.

Tenant protections and affordable housing: sponsor of bills to protect current and converted Mitchell-Lama residents and to bar landlords from using facial-recognition systems against residential tenants.

Gun violence prevention: sponsor of a bill to fund gun-violence victim services through an excise tax on ammunition, and of a bill creating a private right of action for illegal sales of machine guns, assault weapons, and ghost guns.

Criminal justice reform: her official Assembly biography describes her as "the engine behind the 2019 bail reform law which eliminated cash bail for most misdemeanors and non-violent felonies," intended to reduce pretrial incarceration of people who could not afford bail.

positions.summary: Prime sponsor of a bill to fund gun-violence victim services through a new excise tax on ammunition sales, and of a bill creating a private right of action for illegal sales of machine guns, assault weapons, ghost guns, and unfinished frames or receivers.
Prime sponsor of a bill protecting the rights of current and converted Mitchell-Lama residents and of a bill prohibiting landlords from using facial-recognition systems on residential premises.
Prime sponsor of a bill increasing the amount of residential solar energy tax credits available to homeowners.

Prime sponsor of a bill requiring police officers who accompany federal immigration officers on civilian actions to wear and activate body cameras and secure the recordings, and of a bill granting family courts jurisdiction to determine guardianship of minors when a parent faces deportation or removal.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A01290, which would impose an excise tax on ammunition sales to fund a new gun violence impact fund administered by the Office of Victim Services. Referred to the Ways and Means Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A06363, which would prohibit landlords from using facial-recognition systems on residential premises. Referred to the Housing Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.
Prime sponsor of A06432, relating to protecting the rights of current and converted Mitchell-Lama residents. Referred to the Housing Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07810, establishing a private cause of action for certain violations regarding machine guns, assault weapons, disguised guns, ghost guns, and unfinished frames or receivers. Referred to the Economic Development Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A08668, which would require certain elections of public officials to occur on even-numbered years. Referred to the Election Law Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.
Chairs the Assembly's Election Law Committee for the 2025-2026 session and serves as a member of the Housing, Judiciary, Codes, and Ways and Means committees.

Sponsored New York's 2019 bail reform law eliminating cash bail for most misdemeanors and non-violent felonies. In 2025 she went on a 19-day hunger strike to protest proposed rollbacks to that law during state budget negotiations.

researchNotes: Walker is unopposed on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot; Yahemia Harris, who had filed to run, is listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn or disqualified and is not on the general-election ballot. No 2026 campaign website or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response was found for Walker, so priorities and positions are drawn from her official Assembly biography and her 2025-2026 sponsored-legislation record rather than campaign statements in her own words.
